lots.title: Maintenance and extension of the Operational Windstorm Service
lots.description: Maintain and further develop the operational windstorm climate service for the insurance and risk management sector under C3S. Scope includes continued operational delivery of ETC diagnostics based on ERA5, transition to ERA6, geographic extension to Northern (and where feasible Southern) Hemisphere midlatitudes, enhancement of derived products (return periods, cumulated precipitation), AI-based methods for storm detection and generative extension of statistics, maintenance and development of prototype applications and Jupyter notebooks, user engagement, co-designed online demonstrators, training, EQC liaison and L2 user support.
requirements: Ensure continuous operational delivery, maintenance and evolution of the ETC diagnostics currently based on ERA5 reanalysis, including the CDS dataset 'Windstorm tracks and footprints derived from reanalysis over Europe between 1940 to present'.

Maintain and further develop the two prototype applications and the Jupyter Notebooks associated with the windstorm dataset, ensuring they remain fully operational, track any changes to the underlying datasets, and are promptly restored in coordination with C3S in the event of technical issues.

Perform scientific completeness and consistency checks, including validation against known recent high-impact European windstorms, and review/correct post-processing and spatial filtering criteria applied to the ETC diagnostics.
Assess the implications of the diagnostics for use in climate assessment products, in particular the C3S European State of the Climate (ESOTC).

Explore, test and benchmark AI-based methods for the identification, tracking, and characterisation of extra-tropical cyclones and associated windstorms, reproducing the existing algorithm-based diagnostics, ensuring physical consistency, full documentation, and rigorous evaluation against the ERA5-based methodology before any operational implementation.
Provide Level 2 user support by responding to user queries escalated by the C3S User Support team.

Prepare migration of the CDS catalogue entry and associated workflows to ERA6, including targeted testing of storm detection, tracking, and post-processing using initial ERA6 data and an assessment of ETC-diagnostic sensitivity to changes in resolution, model formulation, and data availability.

Extend the service geographically from the current European domain to cover the entire Northern Hemisphere midlatitudes and, where technically and scientifically feasible, the Southern Hemisphere midlatitudes, with methodological consistency.
Add cumulated precipitation associated with windstorm events as a complementary hazard variable alongside wind gusts.

Introduce return period estimates for key variables relevant to windstorm risk, methodologically consistent and suitable for risk assessment applications, delivered on cycles compatible with downstream users (e.g. insurance premium annual review).

Develop and assess methodologies to enhance windstorm statistics for downstream risk and catastrophe modelling; approaches may include UNSEEN-type resampling, synthetic windstorm event generation, perturbation/analogue-based approaches, and AI-based generative methods, benchmarked against ERA5 and evaluated for physical realism and statistical robustness.

Develop and assess extra-tropical storm indicators suitable for both historical reanalysis (ERA5/ERA6) and climate projection datasets (CMIP/CORDEX), based on gridded or regional diagnostics (e.g., exceedance-based metrics, spatial aggregates, persistence, footprint-based indicators) without relying on explicit tracking of individual storms.
Ensure methodological consistency with C3S Atlas products (selected climate models) and adaptability to evolving background climate models and ensemble configurations.

Develop a user engagement strategy with identification of relevant user communities (insurance, reinsurance, EIOPA, catastrophe modelling) including stakeholder interaction, collection of evolving requirements, and co-development of case studies; communicate findings whether positive or negative; deliver lessons learned, best practices and recommendations on scalability.

Transform valuable case studies into co-designed online demonstrators that deliver operational, regularly updated products with a visual component, with backing datasets delivered via the CDS, automatically maintainable after the contract ends, and with fully documented workflows.

Deliver training and dissemination materials co-defined with champion users and ECMWF (webinars, fact sheets, training events), contribute to ECMWF training and capacity-building activities, liaise with the C3S Evaluation and Quality Control (EQC) contractors, and set up and populate a C3S website presence for the service.
Propose a coherent set of deliverables and work packages addressing the above technical tasks (see §7.3 on Deliverables and Milestones).

lots.title: Maintenance and extension of operational storm surge products
lots.description: Ensure continued operational delivery, scientific robustness and strategic extension of the C3S Operational Storm Surge Climate Service. Scope includes operationalising the storm-surge/extreme-sea-level product chain with NRT delivery and QA/QC, ERA6 preparation, AI-based method exploration for surrogate/emulation/post-processing, maintenance and evolution of statistical indicators (percentiles, return periods, confidence bounds), restructuring of the climate-projections component to a broad CMIP6/CMIP7 selection aligned with C3S Atlas, plus training, L2 support, ESOTC contribution and website presence.
requirements: Generate an operational chain to update the current product with NRT delivery and ensure continuous operational delivery of the reanalysis-based products at least of the same quality and resolution as the current ones, with monitoring and timely restoration after issues.

Permit alternative modelling frameworks or updated model versions only if outputs are scientifically equivalent or improved, methodological changes are fully documented, and impacts on historical consistency/uncertainty/interpretation are clearly assessed (continuity not strictly required but must be documented and appropriately versioned).
Subject any proposed change of underlying model to scientific validation, benchmarking against the existing products, and approval by ECMWF/C3S prior to operational adoption.
Implement an operational update cycle with updates at least monthly (or as agreed with ECMWF/C3S) to incorporate newly available reanalysis data and keep the catalogue current.

Implement QA/QC procedures appropriate for operational dissemination (consistency checks, completeness checks, outlier detection, metadata validation, and verification against known historical high-water events where feasible).
Maintain and update CDS catalogue entries, documentation, and user guidance so changes are traceable and reproducible.

Prepare the product chain for ERA6, including impact assessment on forcing fields, resolution and availability; targeted early-ERA6 testing of the end-to-end workflow (forcing → modelling/post-processing → delivery); and a documented sensitivity assessment and migration plan for operational adoption once ERA6 becomes available at scale.

Explore AI-based methods for generation, emulation, acceleration or post-processing of storm-surge and extreme-sea-level products (surrogate/emulation models, AI-assisted post-processing/bias-correction/downscaling, hybrid physics+ML), ensuring physical consistency, rigorous evaluation against existing physics-based products, robustness/stability/operational suitability, and never compromising operational continuity.

Maintain the indicator generation chain and ensure indicators remain consistent across updates (versioning, methodological traceability, backward compatibility where possible); document methods, assumptions, limitations and uncertainty treatment (extreme value methodology, confidence intervals, sensitivity to record length).
Expand indicators as needed by the user community.
Contribute to cross-lot coordination with Lot 1 and deliver joint windstorm–storm-surge products for selected events and regionally aggregated statistics (see §6).

Restructure the climate-projections component so that storm-surge/sea-level indicators are produced and assessed from a broad selection of CMIP6 simulations (and CMIP7 when available) through 2100, aligned with the C3S Atlas philosophy (transparent model selection rules, consistent periods/scenarios, robust ensemble statistics, reproducible processing).

Define and document a model/ensemble selection strategy (eligibility criteria, scenario coverage, temporal windows such as near-term/mid-century/end-century, handling of multiple realizations), and a consistent approach for ensemble aggregation and uncertainty characterisation.

Ensure methodological consistency and traceability between historical reanalysis indicators (ERA5/ERA6) and future indicators derived from CMIP ensembles, with clear separation of drivers (mean sea level contribution vs surge/tide variability) where relevant.

Provide updated training and example workflows (e.g. notebooks demonstrating retrieval, visualisation, detrending, percentile/return-period calculations and interpretation), Level-2 support, C3S website content, and contribute to ESOTC report writing where products are selected for inclusion.

warnings.message: The tender specification document does not contain explicit CPV codes. CPV 73000000-2 (Research and development services and related consultancy services) was carried over from the notice-level main_category on the contract notice, not extracted from the specification itself.

No numeric evaluation weightings or scoring methodology are disclosed inside this Volume II document. §8 provides proposal-section guidance and page limits only; weighted scoring rules (if any) are likely in Volume III or Volume IIIB which are not part of this extraction payload.

Pricing schedule and budget detail are described as being in Volume IIIA (Pricing and deliverables) / Volume IIIB, not Volume II. No price/quantity rows are present to extract; this skill correctly focuses on lot structure and product-requirement seeds.

The 'joint-windstorm-stormsurge-products' seed is cross-lot by design (Section 6 spans both Lots). It is attributed to Lot 1 for seed indexing since the windstorm event catalogue anchors the joint diagnostics, but the work is explicitly coordinated with Lot 2 and should not be double-counted.

Existing notice-level lot metadata only records Lot 2. The tender specification authoritatively defines two lots (Lot 1 Windstorm and Lot 2 Storm Surge) as two separate Framework Agreements under a single ITT reference (C3S2_413_bis), each with its own independent submission. The daemon should treat the lot set emitted here as authoritative for the specification-derived lot structure.

KPI definition (§7.8), L2 support SLA (§7.5, 85% Level-2 tickets resolved within 15 business days), ESOTC contribution (§7.6) and Payment Plan (§7.9) apply to both lots. These are represented as lot-level requirements and evaluation criteria to preserve attribution without duplicating shared sections verbatim.
